clue.text: Preliminary drink suitable if entertaining King Edward I

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or hold, so the word for suitable holds the king inside it

parts.note: apt means suitable
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward, and I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host offers a fitting pre-dinner drink while receiving a medieval king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like amusing but means holding inside; ER is the usual crossword king, here with the numeral I for Edward the First.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite is literally a preliminary one.

clue.text: Chance of success Gray distantly associated with Eton College

definitions.meaning: the likelihood of something good happening, as in a job candidate's chances

definitions.text: Gray distantly associated with Eton College
definitions.meaning: Thomas Gray wrote the 'Ode on a Distant ... of Eton College', so that word is what he links distantly to Eton

explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an English public school; Thomas Gray's 1742 ode views it from afar, hence 'distantly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an outlook or likelihood, and the key noun in the title of Gray's poem.

clue.text: Mediaeval writer about state and church is bishop

indicators.note: the letters for a bishop go round the others, about meaning surrounding here

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
Oman is a state in Arabia
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A historian of the Middle Ages writes about a nation, its church and a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but signals the container; RR (Right Reverend) is a standard crossword bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer is a writer of medieval verse romances, tales of chivalry.

clue.text: Weller senior's nomination for theatre award

definitions.meaning: Sam Weller's father in Dickens's Pickwick Papers has this first name, nomination meaning the name given
the annual Broadway prize for theatre, the Antoinette Perry Award

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nomination' looks like a shortlisting for an award but here means simply a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens character Weller senior bears this first name, and the Broadway award shares it as its nickname.

clue.text: Desert in order to get drink in Japan

parts.note: for, as in 'go for water', means in order to get
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone abandons home to fetch a drink in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to abandon them, a straight synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Do little, say, to identify this street trader?

definitions.text: Do little, say, to identify this street trader?

parts.words: Do little, say, to identify this street trader?
parts.note: Eliza Doolittle in Shaw's Pygmalion sells flowers in Covent Garden; 'Do little' sounds out her surname

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do little' reads as idling, but it is Eliza Doolittle's surname split; she sells flowers on a London street.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the famous street seller of blooms in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.

clue.text: Bare bones of eclogue, originally framed by old poet

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the poet's name as a picture sits in a frame

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet

indicators.note: the start of the word eclogue supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A critic finds the bare outline of a pastoral poem in an old poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bare bones of anything, its essential framework.

clue.text: For example, Richard I was more blunt about it

indicators.note: the word for more blunt goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: cruder means more blunt, rougher in manner
it is crossword shorthand for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: Richard I was a more outspoken king on some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard the Lionheart, King Richard I of England, led the Third Crusade.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I fought in the Third Crusade, making him an example of a holy-war knight.

clue.text: Person watching card-game in centre of New York city

indicators.note: the card game sits inside the trimmed city name
only the middle of the city's name is used, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: Yonkers is a city in New York State
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a game of cards in a New York city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' trims a city name not printed in the clue, dropping its first and last letters; Yonkers lies just north of New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a bystander, a person watching without taking part.

clue.text: A member of hoi polloi is more frequently encountered

definitions.meaning: hoi polloi are the common people, so one of them is an ordinary non-noble person
the comparative of common, meaning met with more often

explanation.walkthrough: The held text 'hot polloi' is an OCR slip; the page prints 'hoi polloi', Greek for the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the masses is a non-aristocrat, and the comparative of common means more usual.

clue.text: One may hope for a good deal from these factories

definitions.text: One may hope for a good deal from these factories

parts.words: One may hope for a good deal from these factories
parts.note: deal is also timber, pine or fir planks, which these factories produce

explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' reads as a bargain, but deal is sawn softwood planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mills that saw logs into planks turn out deal, the softwood timber the clue punningly mentions.

clue.text: Eirenic type, as leading athlete accepting last in race

indicators.note: the leading runner takes in, or accepts, a letter

parts.note: a pacemaker leads a race to set the speed

indicators.note: the final letter of the word race is used

explanation.surface: A peaceable athlete in front lets the last runner in the race pass.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenic type promotes peace, which is what one who brokers reconciliation does.

clue.text: Religious feast Ishmael came out East to organise

indicators.note: out says the letter for East is taken away from the pool
the remaining letters are arranged afresh, organised into the answer

explanation.surface: Ishmael travelled out East to arrange a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: ISHMAEL plus CAME, with one E taken out ('out East'), rearranged ('to organise'), gives the feast. It is 29 September, St Michael's day.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of St Michael and All Angels is a Christian festival and a quarter day.

clue.text: Endlessly examine old wooden post

indicators.note: the word for examine loses its last letter, having no end

parts.note: to study is to examine

explanation.surface: Someone tirelessly inspects an ancient wooden post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like 'tirelessly' but means the final letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an upright wooden post in a timber-framed wall, an old builder's term.

clue.text: An extensive region said to be appealing

indicators.note: the words are spoken, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: a tract is an extensive area of land, giving 'a tract'

explanation.surface: A large stretch of land is said to be attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw others, which is what being appealing amounts to.

clue.text: At end of month, play regularly in way to inspire admiration

indicators.note: the picked letters come after, at the end of, the month

parts.note: August is a month

indicators.note: every other letter of the word play is taken

explanation.surface: At the end of summer, someone plays regularly in an impressive fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'play', L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes acting with majestic dignity, in a way that commands awe and respect.

clue.text: Put up with European bunch upping charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping sends the word for bunch upward, read in reverse

parts.note: a lot is a group or bunch
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A group of Europeans endures a rise in fees.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to bear it, to put up with it.

clue.text: A soothsayer is more godlike

definitions.meaning: one who foretells the future or finds hidden water

explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet who foresees, and the comparative adjective means holier, closer to a god.

clue.text: Lacking confidence, arrange cover for crossing City

indicators.note: the word for arranging cover goes across, round, the other piece

parts.note: to insure is to take out cover against loss
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone nervously takes out an insurance policy for travel through the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insecure is anxious and unsure, lacking self-confidence.

clue.text: Former partner on stage making unreasonable demands

parts.note: ex is a former spouse or partner
acting, performing in a play

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse turned actor is very demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting boss is demanding, requiring very high standards.

clue.text: Foolish description of Dostoevsky hero?

parts.note: Prince Myshkin is the title character of Dostoevsky's novel The Idiot, so an adjective from that title would describe him

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means foolish, and it also comes from the title of the novel about Myshkin.

clue.text: Mine produces this bull's-eye

definitions.meaning: a precious metal dug from mines
the centre ring of an archery target

explanation.definitionFit: The precious metal is mined, and archers call the centre of the target by its name.

clue.text: Spanish fellow following with posh Welsh girl

indicators.note: the fellow comes after the word for with

parts.note: and means with
Al is a man's name, a fellow
U means upper-class, posh
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A man from Spain accompanies a smart girl from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish fellow' looks like the definition, but 'fellow' is AL; the definition is just 'Spanish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is a region of southern Spain, so its adjective is a narrower form of Spanish.

clue.text: New girl's abode oddly is in sultan's palace

indicators.note: new signals the letters remade in a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters of girls

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of abode are taken

explanation.surface: A new girl's home is in the sultan's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes A, O, E from 'abode'; with GIRLS these rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, or the sultan's palace itself.

clue.text: Mournful gent's omitted to propose

indicators.note: the gentleman is left out of the longer word

parts.note: plangent means loudly mournful
the 's links, as in 'gent is'; the word gent is what goes

explanation.surface: A gentleman's sad manner is left out of a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan is to intend or propose a course of action.

clue.text: Disclose sort of acid originating in the earth?

parts.note: to tell is to disclose
uric acid is a kind of acid

explanation.surface: Reveal which acid comes from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Telluric means of the earth, from Latin tellus, the earth.

clue.text: Strange rite in ancient language not all learned

indicators.note: the rearranged rite goes inside the language word
the language name is incomplete, losing its last letter

parts.note: Latin is an ancient language

indicators.note: strange signals the word rite in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange ritual in an old tongue is not understood by all scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the letters of 'rite'; 'not all' cuts the final letter from the language name before the scrambled letters go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means learned people, the scholarly class, so 'learned' as a plural noun works.

clue.text: Come together to swindle bishop's staff

parts.note: to con is to swindle
a verge is a ceremonial rod carried before a bishop

explanation.surface: A thief plans to swindle a cleric out of his crozier.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to meet at a point, to come together.
